chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from 'Umar ibn Aban, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (عليه السلام) saying: Indeed, the knowledge that descended with Adam (عليه السلام) was not raised away, and no learned one dies such that his knowledge goes away.

key_terms.آدَمَ: Adam (عليه السلام), the first prophet with whom this knowledge descended
key_terms.الْعِلْمَ: the divinely bestowed knowledge being discussed in the narration
key_terms.عَالِمٌ: a learned one who bears and transmits knowledge
key_terms.عِلْمُهُ: his knowledge; the knowledge possessed and conveyed by the learned one
key_terms.لَمْ يُرْفَعْ: was not raised away; was not removed

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain the continuity of divine knowledge from Adam (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the divinely bestowed knowledge sent down with Adam (عليه السلام) remains preserved and is not removed from the earth. It indicates the continuity of sacred knowledge through God's chosen learned ones, underscoring the transmission of divine guidance across generations.
